about: The test shelf: the one file that holds the ceiling every test runner of this repo holds a test to, and the tests that are over it.
ceiling_s is the longest a test may run, in seconds. It is read by every runner (tools/internal/testshelf, tools/shelf_reader.py, cmake/TestShelf.cmake, the justfile) and is never raised for a test.

A test over the ceiling is shelved, not rewritten: it stays in the repo, is skipped by the runner that reads this file, and comes back only when someone rewrites it to run fast (the aim for a unit test is milliseconds; the ceiling is only the limit).

An entry id is <kind>:<unit>, or <kind>:<unit>#<case> where the kind has cases. kind is just (a recipe), target (a tools/test_map.json target), pytest (unit: the file name under tools/tests; case: Class, Class.test or test), go (unit: the package under tools/; case: a Test function), gtest (unit: the binary; case: Suite.Test) or ctest (unit: the ctest test name).

Each entry carries its reason (what was measured, over how many runs, and where), and the date it was shelved. A test over the ceiling that is not listed here fails its runner's ceiling; an entry for a test that does not exist fails tools/internal/testshelf.
